scene: Babel BB-ST-3 — End of Souls — complete first draft

source.version_difference: CN has 336 physical lines and no terminal newline; EN Yostar has 337 physical lines because of one additional terminal newline. Both sources contain 122 text-bearing positions at identical physical lines and with the same type sequence: 85 named dialogue lines and 37 narration lines. The 214 non-text control commands match exactly. Speaker names are localized differently in the source files but occupy the same positions. CN is primary for meaning; EN is used to cross-check names and structure.

semantic_differences.description: CN says Theresa also lacks sufficient experience with memory erasure; EN adds 'actually'. Russian follows the CN emphasis.
CN frames the Doctor's hesitation as a long absence of occasions worth celebrating; Russian preserves the shared past and scarcity of celebrations.
CN says Kal'tsit pats the Doctor's back and gently pushes him toward the waiting crowd. Russian retains both actions.
CN specifies a still-unhealed needle wound on the woman's hand; Russian keeps the physical detail.
Both <color=#FF4200> tags and identifier 0091_admin are preserved; full-width parentheses follow the CN payload.
CN 守望者 can mean watcher or guardian. Russian uses 'страж' to retain the protective nuance.
CN refers to prior bandit attacks at the location and dispatching armed security. Russian follows the CN sequence.
CN 好孩子 is an encouraging address; Russian uses 'умница' without adding a gender marker.
CN 阳谋 denotes an overt, not hidden, plan that is nevertheless unavoidable. 'Открытый замысел' is a working rendering and remains a literary-review point.
CN describes the Oracle as residue left after the Doctor's emotions burned away. Russian preserves the burnt-remnant image.
CN explicitly includes the wind rushing through the wheat field and the last scene dispersing to reveal the end of a thread. Russian keeps both images.
The runtime placeholder {@nickname} is preserved exactly.
